Background | Information

Context Import | Astronauts | need | to | wear | spacesuits | whether | they | are | inside | or | outside | the | rocket, | but | the | two | spacesuits | are | actually | different | . | In | - | cabin | spacesuits | are | spacesuits | used | in | the | cabin | of | manned | spacecraft | . | This | spacesuit | is | developed | on | the | basis | of | high | - | altitude | flight | airtight | suits | (referred | to | as | pressure | suits) | in | aviation | . | When | the | pressure | suit | is | inflated | and | pressurized, | it | is | in | an | anthropomorphic | state | . | Wearing | a | pressure | suit, | the | whole | body | can | be | in | the | same | and | uniform | atmospheric | pressure | environment | .

Context Import | If | the | space | suit | is | not | worn | properly, | the | pressure | changes | caused | by | the | rocket | lift | - | off | can | be | extremely | uncomfortable, | which | can | damage | the | DVWURQDXWµV | physical | functions | . | So, | what | effect | low | atmospheric | pressure | has | on | the | human | body?

Context Import | According | to | the | degree | of | low | atmospheric | pressure, | it | can | be | divided | into | three | situations | : | 1 | . | If | it | is | a | mild | low | pressure | , | people | will | not | feel | much | sense, | on | the | contrary, | they | will | feel | more | comfortable | . | For | example, | people | living | in | plateau | will | be | more | strenuous, | but | the | seaside | will | be | more | comfortable | . | 2 | . | If | it | is | moderately | low | pressure | , | people | will | feel | uncomfortable, | the | internal | pressure | of | the | body | will | increase | (compared | to | the | external | pressure), | mild | swelling | will | appear, | and | the | blood | circulation | will | be | poor | . | 3 | . | If | it | is | a | severe | low | pressure | , | people | will | die | because | of | the | high | internal | pressure | . | So | astronauts | need | to | wear | good | space | suits | to | get | on | the | rocket | .
Knowledge  | Introduction

New Knowledge | Atmospheric | pressure | is | so | important | . | In | extreme | environments, | we | need | to | always | pay | attention | to | the | atmospheric | pressure | of | our | environment | to | ensure | our | own | life | and | health | .

New Knowledge | The | current | altitude | can | be | measured | by | atmospheric | pressure, | and | various | altitude | - | related | tools | can | be | made | through | this | feature | . | In | addition | to | the | existence | of | atmospheric | pressure | on | the | surface, | atmospheric | pressure | also | exists | below | the | surface | where | it | can | touch | the | air | . | For | example, | when | mining, | workers | need | to | go | down | to | a | depth | of | hundreds | of | meters, | or | even | thousands | of | meters | .

New Knowledge | Under | a | slightly | higher | pressure, | it | can | make | people | feel | a | sense | of | fullness | in | the | ears, | leading | to | tinnitus, | dizziness, | etc | .; | when | the | atmospheric | pressure | is | greater | than | 7 | Kpa, | it | may | cause | slow | heartbeat, | confusion, | and | even | death | . | Of | course, | the | reality | is | that | even | if | we | go | thousands | of | meters | underground, | there | will | be | no | danger | of | such | high | pressure | . | Make | an | electric | drill | controlled | by | atmospheric | pressure | . | When | the | atmospheric | pressure | reaches | the | set | value, | the | electric | drill | stops | working | .
